title: Probe-driven fanout controller with retroactive rollback levers
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a probe-driven fanout rollout controller that enables retroactive rollback triggers and replayable rollback ledger; backward compatible with existing rollout policies.
description:
Motivation:
Service teams continue to ask for safer, lower-latency canary and A/B experiments that can retroactively revert decisions when slow signals emerge. Existing staged canary controllers rely on forward-only gating; they lack a consistent way to 1) fan out short-lived probe traffic across heterogenous model variants, 2) record time-indexed probe outcomes for retroactive policy evaluation, and 3) trigger deterministic replay rollbacks when post-commit regressions are detected.

This PR introduces the Probe-driven Fanout Controller (PFC) and a lightweight Retroactive Rollback Ledger (RRL). The PFC coordinates probe traffic (synthetic and sampled real requests) across model variants (canary, baseline, shadow lanes) with configurable probe patterns (burst, periodic, stratified). The RRL records probe events and metric snapshots so automated rollback policies can evaluate historical windows and perform deterministic replay-based rollbacks.

Summary of changes (single-string description kept continuous):
- New controller: serving/orchestrator/pfc/controller.go + pfc/scheduler.go + pfc/config.go implement probe scheduling, cohort allocation, and safepoints for fanout phases.
- Retroactive ledger: serving/orchestrator/ledger/ledger.go + ledger/store_sql.go + ledger/compact.go implement an append-only time-indexed ledger with compaction helpers and replay hooks.
- Policy adapters: serving/orchestrator/policies/retro_policy.go adds evaluation hooks for thresholded retroactive rollbacks and windowed scoring.
- Console integration: console/rollouts/ProbeRolloutCard.tsx + console/rollouts/api.ts add UI to visualize probe timelines and a manual rollback/replay action.
- E2E and integration tests: infra/tests/integration/test_probe_fanout.py + infra/tests/e2e/replay_rollback_smoke.py exercise scheduling, ledger replay, and rollback fidelity.
- Docs: docs/rollouts/probe_fanout.md and docs/rollouts/retro_rollback_playbook.md describe configuration and runbook.
- Small API change: new optional field rollout.probePattern on the Rollout CRD (backwards compatible default behavior) and a RolloutStatus.probeTimeline for UI.

Why this is safe: the controller operates under existing rollout admission and only allocates probe fractions (defaults to 0.5% of traffic) unless explicitly configured. Ledger writes are append-only and sharded by rollout ID; compaction runs asynchronously. All changes are feature-flagged under rollout.feature.probe_fanout.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller scheduling and fanout logic implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Ledger append/replay semantics covered by integration tests
- [x] Policy adapter with safe defaults (auto-abort on >20% metric regression in probe window)
- [x] Console UI to surface probe timeline and manual replay/rollback
- [x] Feature flag gated and documented
- [x] Performance sanity: probe scheduler adds <1% CPU to control-plane under 5k active rollouts

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Rollouts without rollout.probePattern continue to behave as before (no probe fanout).
- Rollouts opting into probe_fanout will have small ledger writes; operators should enable compaction cron in Dedicated/Private installer to bound storage.
- The RolloutStatus.probeTimeline is additive and read-only for clients.

Testing notes and CI history (summary):
- Unit: all new unit tests pass (coverage +2.1%).
- Integration: initial run failed on flaky test infra (infra/tests/integration/test_probe_fanout.py) due to timing assumptions; fixed by adding deterministic clock injection.
- E2E: replay_rollback_smoke validated rollback fidelity on a synthetic latency regression scenario.
- Load: controller performance bench shows median scheduling latency 14ms under 2k active probes.

Operational runbook snippet (embedded):
- If a retroactive rollback triggers unexpectedly, the controller sets rollout.status.phase=HOLD and emits rollout.events with a rollback_ticket ID. Use console -> Rollouts -> "View probe timeline" to inspect probe windows; replay can be started from the UI which performs deterministic replay against a frozen input snapshot.

Usage example (Rollout CR snippet):
rollout:
  id: recommend-v2
  model: redwood/gpt-medium:2026-02-01
  probePattern: "stratified(period=5m,fraction=0.005,burst=50)"
  policies:
    - type: RetroactiveThreshold
      window: 30m
      metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 1.20

Notes on follow-ups: ledger retention policy management and cross-region ledger replication are out of scope for this PR (tracked in ENG-2499).
